instructions.cross_packet_rule: Use cross_packet_terms for likely synonyms, owners, consumers, and seams outside this packet.
instructions.family_key_rule: Every assigned raw family key must have exactly one family_key_assignments row and at least one mapped feature.
instructions.objective: Normalize every assigned validated audit atom into an exhaustive local inventory of distinct Puppet Master features, systems, tools, workflows, GUI surfaces, integrations, data models, governance controls, or cross-cutting concerns. Preserve under-specification, contradictions, unknowns, and explicit non-gaps.
instructions.output_rule: Write exactly one strict-schema JSON payload in the assigned output directory and then return PMR1.
instructions.partition_rule: Every atom_id must appear in exactly one feature.atom_ids array; no omission or duplication.
instructions.research_rule: Do not browse in this phase. Give every normalized feature at least one concrete external-research question for the mandatory next phase; do not treat absence of seed queries as permission to omit research.
instructions.scenario_rule: Give every feature at least one falsifiable scenario requirement for later certification.
instructions.split_merge_rule: Split concepts with distinct lifecycle, authority, consumers, or failure semantics. Merge only true synonyms describing the same product concept; record aliases and relationships instead of collapsing uncertainty.

atoms.statement: ResearchRun requires non-empty sources, read_receipts, and citations arrays, creating a baseline evidence floor.
atoms.title: Research runs require source, read, and citation evidence

atoms.statement: ResearchRun does not condition closure_state on synthesis_steps, coverage_report_ref, or failure_reason_code and does not establish referential integrity among sources, receipts, citations, and synthesis references.
atoms.title: Research closure can be asserted without closure proof

atoms.statement: DeepResearchRun composes ResearchRun and constrains mode to the deep constant.
atoms.title: Deep research is a strict mode specialization

atoms.statement: The schema defines a versioned Execution Unit Context object owned by the executor; consumers must reference this field set rather than redefine it, and persisted raw authentication material is forbidden.
atoms.title: Executor-owned context contract

atoms.statement: The root object is closed and requires schema identity/version, execution-unit identity/type, run/node/attempt identity, execution role, operational identity, requested account binding, approval scope, and creation time.
atoms.title: Closed root and mandatory core fields

atoms.statement: The declared properties provide a broad execution-context envelope spanning unit topology, run/node/attempt linkage, roles, accounts, operational identity, action and approval scope, policy snapshots, host and source-control references, safe points, replay/redaction modes, and timestamps.
atoms.title: Execution-context property surface

atoms.statement: Reusable definitions distinguish non-empty strings from nullable non-empty strings and constrain operational identity to a closed object with required identity_id and identity_kind fields.
atoms.title: Reusable identifier and identity definitions

atoms.statement: The excerpt includes the schema's final closing brace and is structurally complete across the assigned range.
atoms.title: Complete schema suffix

atoms.statement: The schema independently validates requested_account_binding, requested_account_id, requested_account_policy, and effective_account_id but defines no conditional invariants between them.
atoms.title: Account binding permits contradictory states

atoms.statement: Execution-unit type and execution role each have bounded enums, but the schema has no cross-field rule defining which role is valid for which unit type.
atoms.title: Unit type and role are independently valid

atoms.statement: Approval scope and permission snapshot are unstructured identifiers with no issuer, subject, run binding, issuance/expiry time, revocation state, signature, or required validation behavior in this contract.
atoms.title: Authorization references lack freshness and integrity semantics

atoms.statement: blocked_sequence and allowed_action_ids are optional and independent, and allowed_action_ids has uniqueness but no minimum cardinality or relationship to blocked state.
atoms.title: Blocked and allowed-action states can conflict

atoms.statement: The redaction_profile and replay_policy enums are defined but not required, and the contract does not specify defaults or the authority/audit consequences of replaying under current policy.
atoms.title: Replay and redaction behavior is optional

atoms.statement: Generic identifiers and references enforce only minLength=1, with no trimming, character grammar, maximum length, URI/reference format, or secret scanning; working_directory and labels/policies remain unconstrained strings.
atoms.title: Non-empty strings remain weak untrusted-input boundaries

atoms.statement: created_at_utc and updated_at_utc validate individual date-time syntax but have no cross-field ordering, expiry, revision, etag, or monotonic-update constraint.
atoms.title: Timestamps do not establish freshness or ordering

atoms.statement: Topology, scheduler, host, source-control, runtime-policy, usage-event, and safe-point links are nullable strings without existence, tenant/run ownership, acyclicity, or lifecycle validation in this schema.
atoms.title: Context references lack topology and recovery integrity

atoms.statement: The description names consumers but this schema does not identify them or define packet creation/update ownership, propagation and invalidation, lookup failure behavior, telemetry, or any GUI presentation semantics; those may exist elsewhere but are unproven in the assigned source.
atoms.title: Consumer, lifecycle, operations, and GUI semantics are external unknowns
